threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You say 'the Tube' instead of 'the underground' and look confused when locals don't flinch at delays.
Last night on the 333, a guy in a full suit tried to impress everyone with magic tricks. Ended up pulling a half-eaten sandwich from his pocket instead.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was living in Neukölln when I saw a guy in a tutu juggling flaming torches outside the Kottbusser Tor U-Bahn station. Just another Tuesday.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a club inside a former beer factory, where you dance on a floor made of old beer crates. It's oddly charming and totally unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A local will quietly assess if the taco truck’s serving up lengua before even glancing at the menu; the newcomers will be awkwardly scanning for reviews.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 on Jones—only passenger shouting at the driver about his 'bad karma'. We just rolled our eyes, but honestly, we all felt it.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can pop into a bar at any hour. Many local spots close by 11 PM, especially during the week. It's not a 24-hour city, despite the vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle to navigate the metro's ticket machines; they always seem to push the wrong buttons, holding up the line.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for a napkin at food stalls, not realising everyone just uses their hands. And the seating is always first come, first served.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken on the 333 last night; must’ve been a late-night vendor at the market. Smelled better than the usual boozy vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a toddler shouting 'Bäcker!' at 8 AM and a neighbor responding with a perfectly timed, 'Ja, komm!'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only here can you find spontaneous raves in abandoned buildings on a Tuesday night, complete with locals handing out homemade snacks.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local by their reaction to the BART delays—an eye roll and a knowing smirk, not panic. Tourists fumble with their phones, unsure what to do next.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a woman singing opera on the 31-Get off at the corner of Turk. Only in SF do people turn a bus ride into a concert.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the pretty squares, but they miss the real charm of the narrow streets where local cats sunbathe in the afternoons.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still struggle to order in the cafés—getting the ‘café con leche’ and ‘cortado’ mixed up is a dead giveaway.
